And Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Balak brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘put a curse on Jacob for me; come and denounce Israel!’
I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the beginning,
Like lame legs hanging limp is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.

verses.text: “As surely as God lives, who has deprived me of justice— the Almighty, who has embittered my soul—

xrefs.text: For Job has declared, ‘I am righteous, yet God has deprived me of justice.

When she reached the man of God at the mountain, she clung to his feet. Gehazi came over to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her soul is in deep distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
“Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,
“Do not call me Naomi, she replied. “Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.

Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”

verses.text: as long as my breath is still within me and the breath of God remains in my nostrils,

xrefs.text: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
But there is a spirit in a man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives him understanding.
Put no more trust in man, who has only the breath in his nostrils. Of what account is he?
Nor is He served by human hands, as if He needed anything, because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else.

verses.text: my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.

xrefs.text: Will you speak wickedly on God’s behalf or speak deceitfully for Him?
But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
Would I lie about my case? My wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.’

verses.text: I will never say that you are right; I will maintain my integrity until I die.

xrefs.text: Then Job’s wife said to him, “Do you still retain your integrity? Curse God and die!”
Though He slay me, I will hope in Him. I will still defend my ways to His face.

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, He said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you and your two friends. For you have not spoken about Me accurately, as My servant Job has.
Acquitting the guilty and condemning the righteous— both are detestable to the LORD.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; justice was my robe and my turban.

verses.text: I will cling to my righteousness and never let go. As long as I live, my conscience will not accuse me.

xrefs.text: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Have you considered My servant Job? For there is no one on earth like him, a man who is blameless and upright, who fears God and shuns evil. He still retains his integrity, even though you incited Me against him to ruin him without cause.”
Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things.
In this hope, I strive always to maintain a clear conscience before God and man.
Hold on to instruction; do not let go. Guard it, for it is your life.
I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles, even though I am nothing.

verses.text: May my enemy be like the wicked and my opponent like the unjust.

xrefs.text: For a time, Daniel, who was also known as Belteshazzar, was perplexed, and his thoughts alarmed him. So the king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.” “My lord,” replied Belteshazzar, “may the dream apply to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your enemies!

Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, since the LORD has held you back from bloodshed and from avenging yourself with your own hand, may your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.
The king asked the Cushite, “Is the young man Absalom all right?” And the Cushite replied, “May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man.”

verses.text: For what is the hope of the godless when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?

xrefs.text: What will it profit a man if he gains the whole world, yet forfeits his soul? Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?
Such is the destiny of all who forget God; so the hope of the godless will perish.
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your life will be required of you. Then who will own what you have accumulated?
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly: “Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who of us can dwell with everlasting flames?”

verses.text: Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him?

xrefs.text: Although they may fast, I will not listen to their cry; although they may offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead, I will finish them off by sword and famine and plague.”
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; even though you multiply your prayers, I will not listen. Your hands are covered with blood.
Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
They cried for help, but there was no one to save them— to the LORD, but He did not answer.
There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.

verses.text: Will he delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?

xrefs.text: Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.
Surely then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.
Pray without ceasing.

verses.text: I will instruct you in the power of God. I will not conceal the ways of the Almighty.

xrefs.text: O God, You have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim Your marvelous deeds.
For this is what the LORD has spoken to me with a strong hand, instructing me not to walk in the way of this people:
Surely you have instructed many, and have strengthened their feeble hands.
It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances just as the LORD my God has commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land that you are about to enter and possess.

verses.text: Surely all of you have seen it for yourselves. Why then do you keep up this empty talk?

xrefs.text: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
“How long will you torment me and crush me with your words?
Is there no end to your long-winded speeches? What provokes you to continue testifying?
For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’
“How you have helped the powerless and saved the arm that is feeble!

verses.text: This is the wicked man’s portion from God— the heritage the ruthless receive from the Almighty.

xrefs.text: For he has oppressed and forsaken the poor; he has seized houses he did not build.
if all this is so, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.
A wicked man writhes in pain all his days; only a few years are reserved for the ruthless.
Woe to the wicked; disaster is upon them! For they will be repaid with what their hands have done.

“Then I will draw near to you for judgment. And I will be a swift witness against sorcerers and adulterers and perjurers, against oppressors of the widowed and fatherless, and against those who defraud laborers of their wages and deny justice to the foreigner but do not fear Me,” says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.text: Though his sons are many, they are destined for the sword; and his offspring will never have enough food.

xrefs.text: You will father sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!
His sons will seek the favor of the poor, for his own hands must return his wealth.
I have seen Ephraim, like Tyre, planted in a meadow. But Ephraim will bring out his children for slaughter.
May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out from the next generation.

verses.text: His survivors will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not weep for them.

xrefs.text: His priests fell by the sword, but their widows could not lament.
So now I will consume Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like that of Jeroboam son of Nebat:

Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: “They will not mourn for him: ‘Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!’ They will not mourn for him: ‘Alas, my master! Alas, his splendor!’
This is what the LORD says: ‘I will bring calamity on you and consume your descendants; I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, both slave and free.

Because of all this, behold, I am bringing disaster on the house of Jeroboam: I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, both slave and free, in Israel; I will burn up the house of Jeroboam as one burns up dung until it is gone!

verses.text: Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up a wardrobe like clay,

xrefs.text: Tyre has built herself a fortress; she has heaped up silver like dust, and gold like the dirt of the streets.
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Your riches have rotted and moths have eaten your clothes.
and consign your gold to the dust and the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines,
Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, speaking with mockery and derision: ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans! How long will this go on?’

verses.text: what he lays up, the righteous will wear, and his silver will be divided by the innocent.

xrefs.text: A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the sinner’s wealth is passed to the righteous.
He who increases his wealth by interest and usury lays it up for one who is kind to the poor.

To the man who is pleasing in His sight, He gives wisdom and knowledge and joy, but to the sinner He assigns the task of gathering and accumulating that which he will hand over to one who pleases God. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

verses.text: The house he built is like a moth’s cocoon, like a hut set up by a watchman.

xrefs.text: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
His confidence is fragile; his security is in a spider’s web.
For the moth will devour them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool. But My righteousness will last forever, My salvation through all generations.”
My dwelling has been picked up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day until night You make an end of me.

He has laid waste His tabernacle like a garden booth; He has destroyed His place of meeting. The LORD has made Zion forget her appointed feasts and Sabbaths. In His fierce anger He has despised both king and priest.

verses.text: He lies down wealthy, but will do so no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone.

xrefs.text: They are exalted for a moment, then they are gone; they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.
How suddenly they are laid waste, completely swept away by terrors!

They will be exposed to the sun and moon, and to all the host of heaven which they have loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped. Their bones will not be gathered up or buried, but will become like dung lying on the ground.
But a man dies and is laid low; he breathes his last, and where is he?

verses.text: Terrors overtake him like a flood; a tempest sweeps him away in the night.

xrefs.text: Sounds of terror fill his ears; in his prosperity the destroyer attacks him.
Terrors frighten him on every side and harass his every step.
Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
And that very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!

Now at midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh, who sat on his throne, to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, as well as all the firstborn among the livestock.

verses.text: The east wind carries him away, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.

xrefs.text: On the wicked He will rain down fiery coals and sulfur; a scorching wind will be their portion.
so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
He never returns to his house; his place remembers him no more.
Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
Before your pots can feel the burning thorns— whether green or dry— He will sweep them away.

verses.text: It hurls itself against him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power.

xrefs.text: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them deep into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment;

Therefore as surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled My sanctuary with all your detestable idols and abominations, I Myself will withdraw My favor; I will not look upon you with pity, nor will I spare you.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail, and escape will elude them; they will hope for their last breath.”
I, the LORD, have spoken; the time is coming, and I will act. I will not refrain or show pity, nor will I relent. I will judge you according to your ways and deeds,’ declares the Lord GOD.”
And as I listened, He said to the others, “Follow him through the city and start killing; do not show pity or spare anyone!

verses.text: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place.

xrefs.text: All who pass by clap their hands at you in scorn. They hiss and shake their heads at the Daughter of Jerusalem: “Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?”
And when this temple has become a heap of rubble, all who pass by it will be appalled and will hiss and say, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?’
When the righteous thrive, the city rejoices, and when the wicked perish, there are shouts of joy.
I will make this city a desolation and an object of scorn. All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds.

This carefree city that dwells securely, that thinks to herself: “I am it, and there is none besides me,” what a ruin she has become, a resting place for beasts. Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
